plan.title: Adipose treated vs control DE, sex- and age-adjusted
plan.analytical_narrative: The input is a single gene-level count matrix (/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv, 12,000 genes x 12 samples, delivered from Salmon) plus a 12-row sample table (/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv) carrying condition (6 treated vs 6 control), sex (F/M) and age (years). The research question is a plain two-group differential expression contrast in human adipose tissue, with the explicit complication that the groups are not matched on age and that sex varies between subjects. The plan therefore does exactly three things and no more. T1S1 establishes the sample structure before any test: blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, sample-distance heatmap and library sizes, each coloured by condition, sex and age; critically it also quantifies how badly age and sex are balanced across treated and control, because if age is strongly confounded with condition the adjusted model cannot separate the two effects and the report must say so rather than present the treatment coefficient as clean. T1S2 fits the count model itself: DESeq2 with design ~ sex + age_centered + condition, covariates entered as fixed-effect design terms (never regressed out of the counts beforehand), age mean-centred, control set as the explicit reference level, contrast named as condition/treated/control, Wald test, apeglm shrinkage of the treatment log2 fold change, BH adjustment at alpha 0.05 with DESeq2's independent filtering left on. Two data facts constrain this step and are stated in it: the counts come from Salmon as a gene-level table with no per-sample quant.sf files and no average-transcript-length table in the inputs, so the length offset cannot be recovered — the model is fitted on the counts as delivered, and the report must state that a shift in isoform usage can masquerade as differential expression; and with 6 per group DESeq2 flags rather than replaces Cook's-distance outliers, so NA p-values must be reported separately from those the independent filter produced. T1S3 refits the same design with edgeR quasi-likelihood as an independent second method — worthwhile here because 6 per group is at the low end and because a 3-term design on 12 samples leaves only 8 residual degrees of freedom, so the two dispersion approaches can disagree. T1S4 assembles the report: the DESeq2 gene table with unshrunken and shrunken log2 fold changes, the MA and dispersion plots, the p-value histogram inspected before trusting BH, the DESeq2/edgeR intersection as the high-confidence set, the counts of both kinds of NA, and a frank statement of power (12 samples, 3-term design) and of the age imbalance. No enrichment step is planned: the question asks which genes differ, not which pathways, and gene sets would be unasked scope.

~ sex + age_centered + condition, counts as delivered without length offset
DE report with MA plot, dispersion plot, method overlap, session info
